title: Electrical and Electronics Engineering Careers (power, control, core)
summary: Core EEE careers cover power generation and transmission, electrical machines and drives, power electronics (EVs, solar, UPS) and control systems. This path suits students who like circuits and machines, and it also shows how GATE, PSUs, higher studies and a switch to IT fit in.
outcomes: PSU or Utility Engineer (via GATE or own exams)

sources.title: GATE 2027 test papers and syllabus – IIT Madras

nodes.title: Circuits, fields and electronics
nodes.summary: Electric circuits, electromagnetic fields, signals and systems, analog and digital electronics, and measurements are the base of every EEE path and a large part of the GATE EE syllabus. Get these strong before you specialise.
nodes.proof: Simulate an RLC circuit's step response in ngspice and match it with your hand-worked solution.

nodes.title: Electrical machines and power systems
nodes.summary: Learn transformers, induction and synchronous machines, then power system basics: per-unit values, load flow, faults and protection. Power plants, utilities, substations and design consultancies ask about these first.

resources.title: GATE 2027 EE syllabus – use as a topic checklist

nodes.proof: Model a small three-bus system, run a fault case and explain which protection would act and why.

nodes.title: Control systems
nodes.summary: Transfer functions, stability, root locus, Bode plots and PID tuning. Control is used in drives, automation, robotics and power converters. Learn it with Simulink so you can see a system respond, not just solve on paper.
nodes.proof: Tune a PID controller for a DC motor model in Simulink and show the step response before and after tuning.

nodes.title: Power electronics and drives
nodes.summary: Rectifiers, DC-DC converters, inverters and motor drives. These skills are used in electric vehicles, solar and battery systems, UPS and industrial drives. Simulate converters before you build them.
nodes.proof: Simulate a buck or boost converter, then plot output ripple against duty cycle and switching frequency.

nodes.title: Tools employers ask for
nodes.summary: MATLAB/Simulink and a SPICE simulator are widely used. Many core firms also ask for reading single-line diagrams, electrical CAD, power system study software or PLC/SCADA basics. These are often paid tools learned in college labs or on the job.
nodes.proof: Finish the MATLAB and Power Systems Simulation Onramps and keep one model you can open and explain in an interview.

nodes.title: One end-to-end core project
nodes.summary: Build one project you can explain fully. For example, simulate solar PV with a boost converter and MPPT, run a fault study on a small grid model, or build a motor speed controller on real hardware. Record your results and what went wrong.
nodes.proof: A short report with your model files, plots and design choices, kept in a public repo or shareable folder.

nodes.title: GATE EE, PSUs and government exams
nodes.summary: GATE EE is used for M.Tech admissions and by several power-sector PSUs for hiring; each advert says whether it uses GATE. UPSC ESE has an Electrical stream, and state power utilities run their own exams. Use only official pages for dates.

resources.title: GATE 2027 test papers and syllabus – IIT Madras

nodes.proof: Solve two years of past GATE EE papers under timed conditions and keep a log of weak topics.

sources.title: IIT Madras announces GATE 2027 dates and syllabus revision

nodes.title: Higher studies (M.Tech, MS, research)
nodes.summary: An M.Tech in power systems, power electronics or control (usually through GATE) leads to design, R&D and teaching roles. Decide early, because GATE prep overlaps with final-year placements. Check eligibility on the official GATE site.
nodes.proof: A shortlist of 5–8 programmes with their admission route and a written plan for your final year.

nodes.title: Interview preparation and applying
nodes.summary: Core interviews test machines, power systems, electrical safety basics, your project in depth and aptitude. Revise from past GATE papers, practise explaining your project, and apply only through official career pages.

resources.title: GATE 2027 test papers and syllabus – IIT Madras

nodes.proof: A one-page resume with your project, plus a 5-minute walkthrough of it you can give without notes.

nodes.title: Honest check: switching from core to IT
nodes.summary: Many EEE graduates move to software jobs. Your maths and problem-solving help, but you still need one language, data structures, DBMS, OS, networks and real projects. It is a full switch, not a shortcut. Embedded and EV software sit in between.

resources.title: GATE 2027 CS syllabus – IIT Madras (checklist of CS fundamentals)

nodes.proof: Two working software projects in a public repo and 100+ solved data-structure problems before you apply.
